The petition is filed by the two petitioners who are presently serving as Inspector of Drugs under the Health and Family Welfare Department, Government of Assam and their services were not regularised because of which they have approached this Court on two earlier occasions being W.P(C)
No. 2135 of 2025 and W.P(C) No. 2137 of 2025, which were preferred by the petitioners, assailing the orders by the department for not regularising their services

entities.text: Health and Family Welfare Department, Government of Assam
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: , the writ petitions came to be dismissed.
However, this Court, while dismissing the matters, had directed the respondent authorities to examine their claims as they had already rendered services for more than 20 years under Regulation 3f.

Pursuant to this, the respondents have issued the impugned order dated 17-11-2025, where it was stated that most sanctioned posts of Inspector of Drugs are now filled through regular appointment and hence there is no administrative requirement to continue temporary or ad-hoc appointments.
Therefore, their services were dispensed with.

The learned Senior counsel for the petitioners submits that against the Judgment and Order dated 27-08-2025, passed in WPC 2135 of 2025 and the other with petition, an intra-Court appeal has been preferred, which is presently pending.
However, no interim order has been passed staying the Judgment and Order dated 27-08-2025.
Under such circumstances, at this stage, the Court considers it appropriate Page No.# 4/4 to issue Notice making it Returnable in four weeks.

Since Mr. D Saikia, learned Advocate General, Assam assisted by Mr. B. Gogoi, learned Additional Advocate General accepts notice on behalf of respondents No. 1 to 5, 7 & 8; Ms. P. Sharma, learned counsel accepts notice on behalf of respondent 6, Notices are waived.
Extra copies will furnish within a period of one week from today.
Issue Notice on the stay prayer, returnable on 18.12.2025.
